What's in Season in November?

November brings some of the coziest ingredients of the year! As the weather gets cooler and the holidays approach, it's the perfect time to embrace seasonal produce that works beautifully in everything from hearty dinners and comforting soups to freshly baked desserts.

Whether you're shopping at your local farmers market or planning your weekly grocery list, choosing seasonal ingredients can help inspire your meals, bring variety to your table, and make the most of fall's delicious flavors. Here are some of the best fruits and vegetables to enjoy throughout November, depending on where you live:

Seasonal Fruits

  • Apples: Perfect for homemade apple cider, apple crisps, cakes, breakfast recipes, and savory chicken dishes.
  • Pears: Delicious in baked desserts, salads, oatmeal, and warm spiced recipes.
  • Cranberries: A holiday favorite for sauces, baked goods, glazes, mocktails, and roasted meats.
  • Pomegranates: Great for adding a bright, juicy finish to seasonal salads, roasted vegetables, and desserts.
  • Citrus fruits: Oranges, mandarins, and grapefruit begin becoming more prominent as winter approaches, bringing brightness to drinks, desserts, and savory dishes.

Seasonal Vegetables

  • Sweet Potatoes: A November staple for casseroles, roasted sides, soups, cornbread, and comforting dinner recipes.
  • Pumpkin + Winter Squash: Butternut, acorn, and other winter squash varieties are wonderful for creamy soups, pasta sauces, roasting, and baking.
  • Brussels Sprouts: Delicious roasted with garlic, maple, balsamic glaze, or crispy toppings.
  • Kale + Collard Greens: Perfect for hearty soups, sautés, and traditional Southern-inspired side dishes.
  • Cauliflower + Broccoli: Great for creamy casseroles, roasted vegetable sides, soups, and easy weeknight meals.
  • Carrots + Parsnips: Naturally sweet root vegetables that work beautifully in roasted sides, stews, and cozy one-pot dinners.

What to Cook in November When You're Short on Time

Between busy schedules, holiday planning, and everything else that comes with the season, November can feel like one of those months when there's simply not enough time to cook. Thankfully, enjoying a comforting homemade meal doesn't have to mean spending hours in the kitchen.

When time is limited, focus on easy November dinner ideas that use simple ingredients, require minimal preparation, and deliver plenty of flavor. Think one-pot pastas, skillet chicken dinners, hearty soups, sheet-pan meals, and casseroles that can do most of the work for you.

Here are a few ways to keep dinner simple:

  • One-Pot + One-Pan Dinners: Choose recipes that cook together in a single pot, skillet, or baking dish for less cleanup.
  • 30-Minute Meals: Keep quick pasta recipes, chicken dinners, and simple rice bowls in rotation for especially busy evenings.
  • Soups + Stews: Make a large pot of soup early in the week and enjoy leftovers for easy lunches or dinners.
  • Sheet-Pan Recipes: Roast your protein and vegetables together with your favorite seasonings for a complete meal with minimal effort.
  • Comforting Pasta Dishes: Creamy sauces, flavorful proteins, and simple vegetables can turn everyday pasta into a satisfying fall dinner.

My favorite shortcut? Keep a few flavor-building ingredients on hand—garlic, onions, fresh herbs, broth, and your favorite seasonings. They make it easier to turn basic ingredients into a delicious homemade meal without overcomplicating dinner.

What to Make Before Thanksgiving

The weeks leading up to Thanksgiving are the perfect time to enjoy simple, comforting meals before the big holiday feast. With grocery shopping, menu planning, and holiday preparations already filling your schedule, everyday dinners should feel easy and manageable.

Instead of making elaborate meals every night, focus on recipes that are satisfying, easy to prepare, and ideally provide leftovers. Cozy soups, one-pot dinners, roasted chicken, pasta dishes, and hearty casseroles are all excellent choices for the days before Thanksgiving.

Easy Meals for Thanksgiving Week

  • Soups + Stews: Prepare a hearty soup that can be reheated throughout the week.
  • One-Pot Pasta Dinners: Perfect for feeding the family without creating a sink full of dishes.
  • Roasted Chicken + Vegetables: A simple, comforting meal that can also provide leftovers for lunch.
  • Easy Casseroles: Assemble ahead of time when appropriate, then bake when you're ready to eat.
  • Rice Bowls + Skillet Meals: Great for using vegetables, proteins, and pantry staples you already have.

Thanksgiving Recipes You Can Prep Ahead

You can also use the days leading up to Thanksgiving to get a head start on your holiday menu. Depending on the recipe, homemade cranberry sauce, pie crusts, cornbread for dressing, certain desserts, and prepared vegetables can often be made ahead.

For casseroles and baked side dishes, check the individual recipe instructions to determine whether they can be assembled in advance or should be baked fresh.

Kitchen Tip: Keep your Thanksgiving-week meals relatively simple and avoid using up ingredients you've specifically purchased for the holiday. A little planning can save you from last-minute grocery runs and unnecessary kitchen stress.

November Meal Planning Tips

November meal planning doesn't have to be complicated! With cooler weather, busy weeknights, and holiday gatherings on the calendar, having a simple plan can make cooking feel much more enjoyable.

Whether you're feeding a family, preparing meals for two, or hosting loved ones throughout the month, these practical tips will help you make the most of your groceries, save time, and enjoy more homemade meals.

1. Plan Around Seasonal Ingredients

Build your weekly meals around ingredients like sweet potatoes, apples, winter squash, leafy greens, and carrots. These versatile ingredients work across breakfast, lunch, dinner, and dessert, making them especially useful for meal planning.

2. Choose a Mix of Quick + Cozy Meals

Not every dinner needs to be an elaborate recipe. Balance your weekly menu with a few quick meals, one or two comforting dishes, and a recipe that makes enough for leftovers.

For example, you might plan an easy chicken skillet for Monday, creamy pasta for Wednesday, and a slow-cooked Sunday dinner to end the week.

3. Cook Once, Enjoy Twice

Choose meals that can easily become something new the next day. Roasted chicken can be used in sandwiches, soups, or rice bowls, while leftover roasted vegetables can be added to pasta, salads, or breakfast hashes.

4. Prep Ingredients Instead of Entire Meals

If traditional meal prepping isn't your thing, try washing and chopping vegetables, preparing marinades, cooking grains, or mixing sauces ahead of time. Having a few ingredients ready can make weeknight cooking significantly easier.

5. Keep Your Pantry Stocked

Stock up on versatile staples like pasta, rice, canned tomatoes, beans, broth, flour, oats, and your favorite spices. These ingredients make it easier to put together comforting fall meals without needing a grocery trip for every recipe.

6. Make Room for Thanksgiving

As Thanksgiving approaches, plan lighter-prep dinners and use ingredients already in your refrigerator or pantry. This helps reduce food waste while leaving more time and energy for holiday cooking.

7. Don't Forget About Leftovers

November is a great month for recipes that reheat well. Soups, stews, casseroles, and certain pasta dishes can make the following day's lunch or dinner much easier. Refrigerate leftovers promptly and freeze portions you won't use within a few days.

Remember: A good meal plan isn't about cooking something new every day. It's about creating a rhythm that works for your household while still making room for delicious, comforting food.
